description: Runs coding agent CLIs, including your own, in terminals inside the window. Through an MCP server, agents start, list, and stop each other, message each other and you, and read each other's terminals.
config.title: Agents
config.yolo: Controls whether agents you start run in YOLO mode. When enabled, an agent's CLI runs with its sandbox off and never asks for approval. When disabled, its sandbox is on where the CLI has one, and it asks before running its own commands and edits, but never before calling Facade tools. An agent keeps the YOLO mode it started with, and the agents it starts inherit it.
config.enabled: Controls whether the agent framework is enabled. When enabled, agents can start, list, and stop other agents through Facade tools. When disabled, agents still start, run, and end as usual, but without Facade tools.
config.timeout: Advanced: the number of seconds Facade waits for things it does not control: a new agent to connect, a stopped agent's process to end, this window to answer an agent's MCP server, terminals to be restored after a reload, and text or keys sent to another agent's terminal to get their turn. It is also how long a task or message can stay unfetched before Facade notifies its sender.
config.launch.arguments: Command-line arguments, by group, in this order: `warmUp`, `connect`, `quiet`, `questions`, `messages`, `yoloOn`, `yoloOff`, `model`, `effort`, `extra` (your own), and `task`. A group you set replaces Facade's; `null` leaves it out. `yoloOn` is used only while YOLO is on and `yoloOff` only while it is off; `warmUp`, `connect`, and `messages` only while the agent framework is on; `model`, `effort`, and `task` only when an agent specifies them. Facade fills in these variables for each agent: `${folder}`, `${repository}` (its main checkout), `${home}`, `${messagesDir}` and `${screensDir}` (where long messages and agents' screens are saved), `${model}`, `${effort}`, `${task}` (the agent's first line, which names its task), `${opening}` (for an agent started through `start_agent`: who it is, and that it should ask through Facade messages, as its warm-up tells it), and others.
config.launch.environment: Environment variables Facade sets for each agent. A variable you set replaces Facade's; `null` removes one of Facade's.
config.launch.unattended: What an agent started through `start_agent`, by another agent or by your script, runs with instead of the launch, so that nothing waits for an answer while no one may be watching. Its `arguments` groups replace the launch's groups of the same name, and its `environment` and `settings` are applied over the launch's. An agent you start from the agent menu runs with the launch alone.
config.launch.unattended.arguments: Argument groups for an agent started through `start_agent`, each replacing the launch's group of the same name. A group you set replaces Facade's; `null` leaves the group out for that agent.
config.launch.unattended.environment: Environment variables for an agent started through `start_agent`, applied over the launch's. A variable you set replaces Facade's; `null` removes it, including the launch's.
config.launch.unattended.settings: Claude Code settings for an agent started through `start_agent`, merged over the launch's settings key by key. `null` removes a key, including the launch's.
config.launch.trust: How Facade trusts the folder where an agent starts, and its whole repository, so that the CLI does not stop to ask whether you trust it: `arguments` are passed for that run only, or `merge` is written into the CLI's own `file`, where it stays. `null`: Facade gives no trust, and the CLI asks in its terminal.
config.launch.enterDelay: Controls the delay, in milliseconds, between typing a line into the agent's terminal and pressing Enter. Without it, the CLI may treat fast typing as a paste.
config.launch.taskDelay: Controls the delay, in milliseconds, after the agent's CLI connects to Facade before its first line, which names its task, is typed into its terminal. Applies only to CLIs that receive their task this way.
config.claude.launch.settings: Claude Code settings for each agent, merged over your own key by key; `null` removes one of Facade's. If one value has a type Claude Code does not accept, Claude Code ignores all of them.
config.claude.title: Claude Code
config.claude.enabled: Controls whether Claude Code is offered in the agent menu and to agents.
config.claude.path: The Claude Code program to run. Leave it empty to use `claude` from your PATH.
config.claude.launch: Advanced: how Facade starts Claude Code. Set only what you want to change: in settings.json, pick a part from the suggestions inside the braces to fill in Facade's default, then edit it; `null` removes one of Facade's. **Agents: Show Agent Launch** shows what each agent is started with now.

config.custom.title: Custom Agents
config.custom: Your own agents, by name: `{ "<name>": { "path": "...", "launch": { ... } } }`. Each starts like a built-in agent, in a terminal of its own. Its launch has the same parts as a built-in's (arguments by group, environment, trust, and delays), but Facade fills in none of them: a group you leave out adds nothing. In arguments, `${mcpConfig}` names a file that holds Facade's MCP server in the `mcpServers` format, for your `connect` group; `${folder}`, `${repository}`, `${home}`, `${messagesDir}`, `${screensDir}`, `${model}`, `${effort}`, `${task}`, and `${opening}` are filled in as for a built-in agent.
config.custom.name: A custom agent's name must be 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes, or underscores, starting with a letter or digit. It cannot be a built-in agent's ID (claude, codex, agy, muse) or a reserved name (human, you, me, facade, all, everyone, init, kernel).
config.custom.path: The program to run: a file path, or a command on the PATH that terminals get.
config.custom.launch: How Facade starts this agent, part by part, like a built-in's launch. Only the groups you fill in are used.
